target_customer: Fans of electronic music and live events, mainly in France and Europe
problem: Finding live electronic music events across scattered sources was hard. Goosebump delivered the best events in a single chat message.
business_model: Ticket referral and event promotion, not confirmed by a source
product_category: Event discovery chatbot, later an iOS app

founders.name: Raphael Doulonne
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as Founder/CEO.

founders.name: Axel Delafosse
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as a former co-founder and CTO of Goosebump. His later role at OpenAI is not a prior employer.

founders.name: Henry Fontanier
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as a Goosebump co-founder.

competitors.name: Live Nation concert finder bot
competitors.what: Facebook Messenger bot for concert discovery and ticket purchase, launched in North America
competitors.funding_then: not applicable, part of a public company

technical_complexity.rationale: A Messenger chatbot aggregating event listings is modest engineering, with effort in data sourcing and curation.

defensibility.rationale: Curated taste and a Facebook community offered some pull, but event data and bots were easy for larger ticketing firms to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Live Nation launched a Messenger concert bot in September 2017 and Ticketmaster ran its own Messenger assistant. Goosebump is listed inactive.

market_need_then: A Hutoma article from October 2017 seen in search results reported 15,000 monthly bot users growing 13% weekly and a Facebook community near 20,000 members; the article itself was not opened.

branding.domain_note: The YC listing points to a m.me/higoosebump Messenger link instead of a website.
branding.brand_signature: A Facebook community of electronic music fans that preceded the bot, per a secondary snippet
branding.community_and_virality: Search snippets from an October 2017 Hutoma article describe a Facebook community of about 20,000 members that the bot grew from; not opened directly.

brand_strength.rationale: An evocative name tied to the feeling of live music and a community that predated the product, but only secondary snippets support the community claim.

pivots.why: Not stated; a December 2017 Medium article seen in search results says the product moved from a Messenger bot to an app

outcome_analysis: Goosebump grew out of a Facebook music community and became a Messenger bot in the Summer 2017 YC batch, then reportedly moved to a standalone iOS app. Messenger bots proved a weak channel and Live Nation and Ticketmaster launched their own concert bots, but no source states why Goosebump stopped. The company is now inactive, so the platform dependency factor is an inference from the product history.
notes: The directory website is a Messenger link that redirects to a Messenger login page, so no site could be read. The Dealroom page returned HTTP 429 when fetched; the two seed amounts of about $170K and $125K come from a search summary that called the table garbled with no dates or investors, so both rest on a single database and are weakly supported. The Medium article returned 403 and the community and traction figures come from search snippets. The pivot date is only a year. The Live Nation bot is dated about three months after the S17 batch start.
